[1] 238.4596 232.4340 239.3424 251.2552

[1] 109.2500 128.9256 126.8813 136.8558

> Blk_199C
[1] 227.9699 228.3370 223.6940 234.4604

df = melt(data.frame(Blk_103C,Blk_624C,Blk_613C,Blk_199C,
                     Year=c("2012","2013","2014","2015")),
                     variable.name="BlockNo")
p <- ggplot(df, aes(Year, value, fill=BlockNo)) + 
     geom_bar(position="dodge",,stat="identity") +
     geom_text(aes(label=c(round(Blk_103C,2),round(Blk_624C,2),round(Blk_613C,2),round(Blk_199C,2))),hjust=1.1, vjust = 0.9, size=3.0)+
     ggtitle("Yearly Water Consumption in Years 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015 for different blocks")  +
     labs(x="Year",y="Consumption Levels (m^3)")
p

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: how to align those values properly at the top of the bar with hjust and vjust
parts:
Your example is not reproducible, so let's try one:

set.seed(2530)
DF <- data.frame(A = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 1000, replace = TRUE),
B = sample(letters[1:2], 1000, replace = TRUE))

library(dplyr)
DFsumm <- DF %>% group_by(A, B) %>% summarise(freq = n())

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(DFsumm, aes(x = A, y = freq, fill = B)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
geom_text(aes(y = freq + 3, label = freq),
position = position_dodge(width = 0.9))

Does that do what you want?

BTW, a useful reference for standard ggplot2 graphics, apart from the
on-line help pages, is Winston Chang's excellent "R Graphics
Cookbook", published by O'Reilly, which contains several variations on
this type of example. You can also look to the companion site
http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/, although this particular example is
not covered there.

Dennis
